title: Biblical Commentary on the Books of the Kings (Clark's Foreign Theological Library)

verification_log.method: Downloaded the OCR text of the 1872 translation

pp. 473–475: the reform cannot all fall within the eighteenth year (against Ussher's placing of the Passover at its close); the narrative groups by subject; idolatry's removal began earlier (2 Chr 34:3); pp. 478–479 (notes): the "book of the law" is the Temple copy of the Pentateuch, not a separate collection; de Wette conceded this as the first certain trace of the Pentateuch; "find" is not "forge"; on 22:20 "gathered to his fathers" is used also of death in battle, "in peace" = without seeing Jerusalem's devastation; pp. 493–496: Josiah opposed Necho to keep Judah from Egyptian control; Herodotus's Magdolos is a confusion with Megiddo, not the Egyptian Migdol (against Movers); Necho probably came by sea to Acco; Chronicles does not affirm that Josiah died in Jerusalem
